before.stem: ww Which of the following is NOT an anatomical feature that prevents against gastric reflux:
options: The diaphragmatic pinchcock effect on the oesophagus 4%
Intra-abdominal pressure which maintains the oesophagus in a state of collapse when empty 15%
The angle of His formed at the junction of the oesophagus and gastric fundus 6%
Gastric mucosal rosette-like folds at the gastro-oesophageal junction 10%
The striated lower oesophageal sphincter muscle
before.explanation: The lower oesophageal sphincter is not a distinct muscular structure composed of skeletal muscle like the upper oesophageal sphincter. The lower oesophageal sphincter is formed from a high-pressure zone of smooth muscle, located at the gastro-oesophageal junction. Vv Oesophagus (Abdominal) ANATOMY / ABDOMEN / GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT

before.stem: ww A patient with known inflammatory bowel disease presents to ED complaining of severe abdominal pain and diarrhoea. Imaging shows a flare up primarily affecting the rectum. Which of the following nerves is most likely responsible for transmission of pain from the rectum:
before.explanation: The visceral afferent innervation of the rectum is transmitted by way of the pelvic splanchnic nerves, which also provide parasympathetic supply. Sympathetic nervous supply to the rectum is from the lumbar splanchnic nerves (L1, L2) and the inferior mesenteric plexus (upper rectum) and hypogastric plexuses (middle and lower rectum). v

after.stem: A patient with known inflammatory bowel disease presents to ED complaining of severe abdominal pain and diarrhoea. Imaging shows a flare up primarily affecting the rectum. Which of the following nerves is most likely responsible for transmission of pain from the rectum:
warnings: Source page and external anatomy reference reviewed; remains an unapproved OCR draft.
after.explanation: For the source's intended hindgut visceral-afferent formulation, pelvic splanchnic nerves carry visceral afferents from the rectum and also provide parasympathetic supply; the exact pathway can vary with rectal level and pain type.
after.learningNote: For the source's intended hindgut visceral-afferent formulation, pelvic splanchnic nerves carry visceral afferents from the rectum and also provide parasympathetic supply; the exact pathway can vary with rectal level and pain type.
after.highYieldNote: For the source's intended hindgut visceral-afferent formulation, pelvic splanchnic nerves carry visceral afferents from the rectum and also provide parasympathetic supply; the exact pathway can vary with rectal level and pain type.
after.mnemonic: Pelvic splanchnics: S2–S4 to hindgut and pelvic viscera.

memoryAid.coreFact: Pelvic splanchnic nerves carry visceral afferents from the rectum and parasympathetic fibres to hindgut/pelvic organs; do not read this as an exclusive route for every rectal pain fibre.
memoryAid.mnemonic: Pelvic splanchnics: S2–S4 to hindgut and pelvic viscera.
memoryAid.sourceLabel: NCBI Bookshelf: Anatomy, Abdomen and Pelvis, Splanchnic Nerves

evidence.externalFinding: NCBI states that pelvic splanchnic nerves carry visceral afferents and supply the rectum; the caveat preserves level-dependent nuance.

before.stem: w Which of the following lies immediately medial to the second part of the duodenum:
before.explanation: The descending (second) part is just to the right of the midline, extending from the neck of the gallbladder to the lower border of vertebra L3 and lying lateral to the head of the pancreas. This part contains the major duodenal papilla which is the common entrance for the bile and pancreatic ducts. ; ? Vv

after.learningNote: The head of the pancreas lies immediately medial to the second part of the duodenum.
